In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the amido-bridge in the amido-organometallics is a good ligand for the polymerization of ethylene and 1-octane, and that the polymerization activity of the amido-zirconocene is highly dependent on the type of the trialkyl aluminium applied.
the amido-bridge in the amido-alkyl zirconium complex 1 is not a good bridging ligand for the formation of active catalyst for ethylene polymerizations.
the amido-bridge in 2a and 3a is beneficial to ethylene polymerization, but the presence of an amido-bridge is not a prerequisite for high activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the amido- and imido-bridged complexes (1) and (CpSiMes(2)NCp)Zr(CH(3))(B(C(6)(F)(5))(4)) (6) (Mes = 2,4,6-Me(3)C(5)H)(2)) were highly active for ethylene polymerizations in the presence of MAO or Al(2)Me(6).
the binuclear complexes 2b, and 3b showed higher activities than the mononuclear complexes 3a, and 5.

the amido-bridge zirconocene (CpSiR(2)N)Zr(CH(3))(R = Me or Ph) is a versatile catalyst for ethylene polymerizations, and the catalytic behavior of this catalyst is greatly influenced by the nature of the trialkyl aluminium cocatalysts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the amido-alkyl complexes 2a and 3a are highly active catalysts in the presence of MAO and trialkylaluminum cocatalysts.
the binuclear zirconium complex 2b showed higher catalytic activity than the mononuclear zirconium complex 3b for ethylene polymerizations.
the amido-bridge zirconium complex 1 is a versatile precursor for preparing various zirconium catalysts for ethene polymerization.
